definitions.explanation: Punishment from heaven or the gods for wrongdoing. Used both literally in religious/traditional contexts and figuratively to express that someone deserved their misfortune.

examples.japanese: あんなことをしたら{天罰|てんばつ}が{当|あ}たるよ。
examples.english: If you do something like that, you'll be punished by heaven.

examples.japanese: {悪事|あくじ}を{重|かさ}ねた{結果|けっか}、{天罰|てんばつ}を{受|う}けたのだと{人々|ひとびと}は{噂|うわさ}した。
examples.english: People whispered that it was divine punishment for all the evil deeds committed.

notes:
Composed of {天|てん} (heaven) + {罰|ばつ} (punishment). Expresses the idea that wrongdoers will eventually face retribution from a higher power. In modern usage, it is often used semi-figuratively to mean "serves them right" or to warn someone that their bad behavior will catch up with them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天罰|てんばつ}が{下|くだ}る — divine punishment descends
- {天罰|てんばつ}が{当|あ}たる — to be struck by divine punishment
- {天罰|てんばつ}を{受|う}ける — to receive divine punishment
- {天罰|てんばつ}てきめん — swift and sure divine retribution

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {罰|ばつ} — punishment; general term, not necessarily divine
- {報|むく}い — retribution, karma; consequence of one's actions, without the "heavenly" connotation
- {天誅|てんちゅう} — divine retribution; stronger, more archaic, historically used to justify executing wrongdoers
